04/26/26 Update: Since MFP is telling all of us who hate this atrocious update to ‘deal with it’, I have cancelled my subscription so it doesn’t renew again and have gone to Cronometer. It acts like MFP used to but I find its food database more accurate and the barcode scanning is free! I have had to use AI to help with how I want it setup but so far I like it. So once you make changes on the new screen then you have to go back to the Today screen to see how your change effected either your calories or a particular macronutrient. You get to continue the back and forth until you get your numbers where you want them. Such a fun waste of time!

4. There doesn’t seem to be a way to remove the Healthy Habits section from the Home page. I don’t want to see it but now I get to.  Yay!

What used to take me a few minutes to log food from day to day has now become a complete cluster. Nice work, MFP!

lowStarReviews.title: Simply Unusable
lowStarReviews.text:
The recent complaints are not a result of users being unable or unwilling to adapt to change. It’s a colossal failure.   MyFitnessPal used to be one of the best nutrition and calorie tracking apps with a utilitarian UI: fast, intuitive, and built for efficient calorie and macro tracking. The at a glance layout was phenomenal. The April update has stripped away much of what made it valuable. The clean, functional interface has been replaced with bloated, cluttered screens, extra taps, buried tools, and generic AI slop that add noise instead of value. Features like easy logging, easy copying across days or meal to meal, moving items between meals by long pressing the item, easy access to favorites/recents, clear macro visibility even as your scroll, and streamlined navigation have all been taken away in favor of a cartoonish oversized UI that serves as a home page that you have to navigate away from to log or view data, and constantly having to back out to compare the days meals and breakdown. What was once a practical tracker now feels like a bloated, gamified content platform. Both long time and new users don’t need graphics, oversized sections, and motivational fluff, we need ease of use, clarity, and control. Instead of improving the core product (like allowing for stacking meal headers with macro breakdowns as you scroll to compare % across meals for example), the redesign sacrificed usability for a home page look no one asked for. 

I’ve already cancelled my premium subscription and downloaded competitor apps; and unless the update is rolled back or the old UI offered as an option with all of its features to revert to, I will not be renewing and definitely will not use as a free product, as I can only imagine the ad bloat to the already useless home page. 

I truly hope that Francisco Partners take note of the backlash, especially now that they’re pursuing valuation and potential sale.

I’ve been using MyFitnessPal since 2013, and have used it consistently almost every day for the last 3 or so years. The latest update completely misses the mark. Logging meals now feels unnecessarily complicated, with extra steps that slow everything down instead of streamlining it. For an app that’s supposed to make tracking easier, it’s doing the exact opposite.

One of the most annoying changes is how it handles frequently logged foods. Before, it would actually learn your habits and organize your usual meals in a way that made sense. Now? It’s like starting from scratch every time. The foods I consistently eat are harder to find, poorly organized, or just not prioritized at all. It completely defeats the purpose of building a routine.

The interface itself is also less user-friendly. Things that used to be simple and clearly laid out are now buried, rearranged, or just harder to navigate for no real reason. It feels like change for the sake of change—not improvement.

Overall, this update took a solid, reliable app and made it clunky and inefficient. If the goal was to enhance the user experience, it seriously missed. Hopefully they listen to user feedback and fix it, because right now it’s a downgrade in every way.

These are just my thoughts after 1 day with the new version. lowStarReviews.title: NEW UPDATE IS GOD AWFUL
lowStarReviews.text:
The food diary is the most important part of this app. The new update has removed the diary tab and instead integrated it in a less effective way in the "today" tab, damaging the user experience.

The meals shown grouped in the today tab ("... and 8 more") instead of showing all entries per meal at once is clunky and serves only as a barrier to what most people want, which is to see their full food diary easily and instantly when opening the app. Now, you have to enter a separate page to see the full diary. The full diary should have its own tab, serving as the main focus of the app.

Logged items are now shown each on individual cards that make grossly ineffective use of screen real-estate by being far too large and filled with empty space/padding. At most, 7 items fit on the screen at once, when before, at least 12 could easily fit. The cards need to be condensed, or at least, the option to switch the appearance to a condensed view should be provided.

The new app experience is extremely disappointing. It's not about "taking time to get used to", it's that the app's main focus, the food diary, has been ruined by being converted to a list of gigantic, space-consuming cards and relegated behind a pointless "view all" button. There isn't a single time when I wouldn't want to view my entire daily food diary at once - it's the whole point of the app.

The only thing most people are interested in seeing when they open the app is a summary of nutrition at the top, followed by all their logged items of the day displayed in a meal-separated, space-efficient list that fits as many items on the screen at once as possible without being overly condensed. Kind of like... the way the diary looked before...

This update does nothing but demonstrate a grand disconnect between the MyFitnessPal team and the user experience.

lowStarReviews.title: Ruined By New Update
lowStarReviews.text:
I have been a loyal user for over 15 years, and this is by far the most disruptive and frustrating change I have ever experienced.

The new layout is not functional. Key features that made the app efficient and user-friendly have either been removed or made significantly more difficult to use. For example, I can no longer view individual macros for each meal at a glance—something that is essential for anyone seriously tracking nutrition. Additionally, I am noticing inconsistencies and inaccuracies in macro totals across different sections, which raises serious concerns about the reliability of the app.

One of the most frustrating changes is the removal of the ability to copy an entire day’s food log to another day. This was a core feature for users who maintain consistent, repetitive meal plans. Being forced to copy meals individually is unnecessarily time-consuming and makes the app far less practical for daily use.

The next most upsetting feature taken was the barcode scanning. Just truly insane. 

These changes are not improvements—they are obstacles. Longtime users like myself rely on efficiency and accuracy, and this update has significantly compromised both. Quite frankly, it reflects a lack of understanding of how your most dedicated users actually use the app.

After 15 years of consistent use, I never expected to consider leaving MyFitnessPal. However, if these issues are not addressed and functionality is not restored, I will be closing my account and transitioning to a different platform.

I strongly urge your team to reconsider these changes or provide an option to revert to the previous version or feature set without making users pay for ‘premium’ versions.

lowStarReviews.title: Misleading Billing & No Refund Support
lowStarReviews.text:
I downloaded WalkFit App expecting a simple walking app, but what I didn’t realize at the time was that it included a recurring subscription. There was no clear reminder or notification before I was charged again.

Like many busy people, I didn’t catch it until a large charge hit my account. I hadn’t used the app at all—not even once. I actually had to redownload it just to figure out where the charge came from.

I immediately reached out to request a refund, explaining that the app hadn’t been used. Unfortunately, their policy is extremely strict, and they refused to issue any refund.

This experience left a really bad impression. Transparency around subscriptions and billing matters, especially when it comes to recurring charges. I would strongly encourage anyone considering this app to double-check the subscription terms and set reminders, because you may not get any flexibility if something goes wrong.

lowStarReviews.title: Very buggy and flawed
lowStarReviews.text:
When I first subscribed to this app, it was very solid with just a few issues. However over time it has become very problematic and difficult to use. Here are some of the issues that I have encountered:

* The typed in text has been difficult to read and has a strange swirl pattern to it.
* The default setting for many input meals are often very off. They are usually too small (such as one cracker versus standard serving) or too large (over 1000 calories for something that should be 100 - 200 calories).
* Many meals or snacks are often given a poor rating for invalid reasons (peanuts are rated poorly cause they contain 1 gram of natural sugar!) 

There are many more issues that I have not covered. While this app does have some strengths like its accurate meal prediction using photos, there are too many issues for an app that requires a subscription. I am not sure how these issues have not gone unnoticed by the developers as they are very obvious and have been around for several months. If these issues are ever resolved, I will update my review, but I will most likely be moving to a new nutrition tracking app in the future.

Please make the app options consistent between devices. Please fix the memory of notices between devices.
